picks.title: 10k sign petition demanding legislation on AI firms to disclose training data
picks.excerpt: A petition backed by authors and publishers has passed 10,000 signatures, calling for a statutory requirement that AI companies disclose the copyrighted works in their training data. It escalates the UK trade's push for transparency-first AI regulation.
picks.rationale: The freshest hard news in the pool, and the first time the trade's transparency demand has a number attached — 10,000 signatures is the threshold that forces a formal response.

picks.title: Authors need transparent AI policies, if only to protect themselves
picks.excerpt: Novelist Jamie Fewery argues that writers should publish an explicit personal AI policy — what they use, what they refuse — as basic professional self-defence in a market now primed to accuse. A practical craft-and-disclosure playbook rather than a manifesto.
picks.rationale: Turns weeks of AI-accusation headlines into one concrete task a writer can finish tomorrow: publish the policy before someone else writes it for you.

picks.title: Commonwealth Foundation to delay Short Story Prize submissions after AI controversy
picks.excerpt: The Commonwealth Foundation is postponing 2027 Short Story Prize entries until January and reviewing its processes after allegations that AI was used in the 2026 competition. Literary prizes are being forced to rewrite submission rules around AI.
picks.rationale: Replacement for the janefriedman ChatGPT-style pick (already published 2026-08-06). The curator's designated reserve backfill: an AI allegation has now moved a flagship international prize's calendar, which is the first concrete process cost a literary prize has paid.

picks.title: Spammers and Scammers: What to Do When Your Book Is Sold Under a False Name
picks.excerpt: ALLi's scam-watch series walks through the identity-hijack economy now supercharged by cheap generative output: fake author names, cloned titles and AI-padded listings sold on major retailers. Includes the takedown steps indie authors can actually run.
picks.rationale: Names the failure mode cheap generation actually created for indie authors and hands over the takedown procedure, not another warning about slop.

picks.title: News Podcast: Literary Agents Update Ethics Rules; Seven-Figure Deal Shelved Over AI Claims; Study Examines AI Books on Amazon
picks.excerpt: The Association of American Literary Agents rewrites its Canon of Ethics to let agents work more closely with indie authors and to govern marketing services — but leaves out any rule on how agents and editors may use AI on client manuscripts.
picks.rationale: Replacement for the Princeton/Cashmere pick (already published 2026-08-04). Card is written on the Canon of Ethics segment, which is never-published: the agent side of the trade rewrote its rulebook and left the one AI question everyone is arguing about blank.
